analysis.title: October 2026 FOMC Recap
key_insights: The FOMC held the target range at the October 28 meeting and made few statement changes. The economy was upgraded from "solid" to "strong" with the description of spending, investment, productivity and the labor market unchanged.

The statement added a line that accumulating more information will help the Committee set the policy stance for a timely return to 2 percent inflation. MUFG reads this as a possible first sign of a shift from Powell's "data dependence" toward Warsh's "frameworks" model.

Lisa Cook dissented in favor of a hike. Beth Hammack's dissent was expected. Lorie Logan and Neel Kashkari did not dissent, which MUFG attributes to very low market-implied hike odds given their financial-markets backgrounds.
MUFG expects Logan and Kashkari to vote for a hike in December if inflation stays above target and financial conditions stay relatively loose.
Chair Warsh did not repeat "inflation is a choice" and focused on financial conditions. He said conditions have tightened, crediting the September action, but did not call them tight.

Warsh said higher rates and tighter conditions are showing up through the availability and cost of credit, which is the transmission channel from policy to activity. MUFG agrees and sees heightened rate sensitivity in tech investment.
MUFG says the current FOMC may not lean on the "long and variable lags" argument, because inflation expectations are anchored and tighter conditions are already restricting credit.

Warsh stressed economic strength, but most members do not think the economy is running too hot. If stronger activity reflects productivity and higher potential growth rather than excess demand, the case for an aggressive hiking cycle is weaker.
Warsh noted updates to the 2027 and 2028 meeting schedule and progress by the task forces. A productivity task force update could come as early as November 16, and a balance sheet update in Q1 2027.

The post-FOMC curve steepening supports MUFG's view that longer-term rate moves reflect a re-rating of growth and term premium rather than inflation. The Fed is not signaling urgency to hike at every meeting.

Strong 10-year and 30-year auctions, Treasuries rallying through a hot CPI print and several sizeable rallies in October suggest investors are more willing to buy dips. MUFG sees duration as better supported than earlier in the cycle.

Markets price roughly an 80% chance of a 25bp hike in December versus MUFG's 55%. MUFG says December is not a done deal, citing the election, incoming data, financial conditions and inflation expectations.

sector_views.rationale: MUFG sees heightened interest rate sensitivity in tech investment as tighter credit conditions feed through.

macro_indicators.reading: Held unchanged at the October 28, 2026 meeting
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed paused after the September hike. The statement upgraded the economy to "strong" and added language on gathering information before setting the policy stance.
Market pricing is well above MUFG's own estimate, leaving MUFG below market conviction on a December hike.
MUFG sees December as uncertain, depending on the election, data, financial conditions and inflation expectations.

macro_indicators.reading: Cook voted to hike, Hammack dissented (expected)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Two hawkish dissents. Logan and Kashkari could join them in December if inflation stays above target and financial conditions stay loose.

risk_factors: Inflation staying above target with loose financial conditions could bring more hawkish dissents and a December hike.
The election, incoming data, financial conditions and inflation expectations could change the December outcome.
Higher rates and tighter credit may weigh on rate-sensitive activity such as tech investment.
vol_and_positioning: Strong 10s/30s auctions, Treasuries rallying through hot CPI and several sizeable rallies in October point to investors buying dips in duration.
